authors: design agent for the special-structure lead sweep, unfrozen draft

links.lead: LEAD-EXO-lattes-xline-dynamics (proposed, candidate C3 of family-C report)
links.note: Toy-scale closure check on planted scalars. No deployed key, no cost claim against rho; a k-independence and orbit-length check only.

question: On toy prime-field curves with a point P of prime order l coprime to d, is the multiset of irreducible-factor degrees of phi_d^(n)(X) - x(kP) over F_p the same for every k at a matched curve (d in {2,3}, n<=4, 50 resampled k), and does the forward x-orbit of x(Q) under a CM Lattes map have the length predicted by the multiplicative order of its eigenvalue?

claims.text: For P of prime order l not dividing d, the factor-degree multiset of phi_d^(n)(X) - x(kP) equals the cycle type of Frobenius on E[d^n], for every k not 0 mod l (exact computation, per cell).
The multiset does not depend on k at a matched curve, so the x-line preimage tree carries no information about k beyond what the curve gives.
claims.if_supported: closure of LEAD-EXO-lattes-xline-dynamics at toy scale: no k-dependence in any cell
claims.if_not_supported: any k-dependence at matched curve falsifies the closure; the lead reopens and the cell goes to a root-cause review

claims.text: The same detector separates k classes when d divides ord(P) (positive control) and does not separate shuffled labels (negative control).
claims.if_supported: the null in C2 is not a blind-detector artefact

claims.text: On CM curves with j in {0,1728} the x-orbit period of x(Q) under phi_alpha equals the least m with lambda^m = +-1 mod l, and is at least log(l)/log N(alpha) up to the stated sqrt bound.

hypotheses.statement: H0 (lead's disposition, closed_obstructed): at matched curve with ord(P) prime and coprime to d, the degree multiset is identical for all sampled k. H1: some cell has two k with different multisets.
hypotheses.mechanism: roots are x(k'P + T), T in E[d^n], k'=k d^-n mod l; Frobenius fixes k'P so the orbit structure on roots is that of Frobenius on E[d^n], a curve invariant.

arms.description: k-free reference: predicted multiset = cycle type of Frobenius on E[d^n], derived by the checker from fixed-point counts of E[d^n](F_{p^j}) (PARI ellgroup), no polynomial factored
measured factor-degree multiset of phi_d^(n)(X)-x(kP), 50 resampled k per cell, prime-order P
second independent resample of 50 k at the same cells, different seed; only the k draw differs
cells where d divides ord(P) (cyclic d-part), same code path; multiset must split by class of kP mod d^n E(F_p); also x(kP) itself through the same record writer
positive-control records with the k-class labels permuted uniformly at random, same separation test; false-positive rate must stay at or below alpha
x-line orbit of x(Q) under iterated phi_alpha (rational map, no group law) on j=0 and j=1728 curves, against the eigenvalue prediction

positive.expected_detection: every positive cell yields >=2 distinct multisets that partition exactly by class of kP in E(F_p)/d^n E(F_p) up to sign; orbit comparator fed lambda^m=1 without the sign quotient must mismatch on every curve where -1 is in <lambda>

null_population.description: positive-control records with the k-class labels permuted uniformly at random; the labels carry no information by construction
null_population.generator: Fisher-Yates permutation of class labels, seed 20261104, applied to the recorded positive-control multisets
null_population.why_n: 999 permutations give min p = 0.002 below alpha/m = 0.0125

factors.name: prime_p
factors.how: p in {1009, 2003}; CM arm uses p in {1009, 2017, 4093} (p = 1 mod 12 needed for j=0 and 1728 to be ordinary)

factors.name: curve
factors.how: 3 curves per prime found by scanning (a,b) in lexicographic order for ord(P)=l prime, l>16; the same curve for every k in the cell (matched curve)

factors.name: depth_n
factors.how: n in 1..4 (d=3, n=4 on one curve per prime only)

factors.name: ord_P_divisible_by_d
factors.how: false in the candidate and A/A arms (ord P = l prime, l not dividing d); true only in the positive-control arm

factors.name: labels
factors.how: true class labels versus permuted labels, negative control only

factors.name: k_draw
factors.how: k_i = SHA-256(seed||cell||i) mod l, rejecting 0 and duplicates up to sign, independent of arm

factors.name: target_polynomial
factors.how: numerator minus x0 times denominator of x([d^n]X), taken from the runner's own division-polynomial recursion

factors.name: factoring_code
factors.how: runner: Rust distinct-degree factorisation by Berlekamp Q-matrix; checker: PARI factormod; no shared code

factors.name: threads
factors.how: 1 thread; the metric is exact so the clock is not read

factors.name: host_load
factors.how: recorded per row; affects nothing counted

comparisons.threshold: n_distinct = 1 in every cell and multiset equal to the Frobenius cycle type

seed_derivation.note: curve scan seed 20261101; k set A 20261102; k set B 20261103; label permutations 20261104; CM Q draws 20261105; all fixed before any data

instance_sampling.rule: curves by deterministic lexicographic scan; k by SHA-256 expansion of the seed list; independent of arm

blinding.how: the analysis is a deterministic equality test on recorded multisets; no judgement to steer

power.note: C2 is an exact equality, not a sampled test: one differing pair falsifies it. The permutation test of C3 uses 999 label permutations, min p = 2/(999+1) = 0.002 < 0.05/4 = 0.0125. Power of C2 to see a k-dependence is stated by the positive control, where the dependence is a Z/d^n class: 50 draws miss a class of density 1/3 with probability (2/3)^50 ~ 1.6e-9.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: gp 2.15.4 probe: d=3 n=3 (deg 729) under 0.2 s per factorisation, n=4 (deg 6561) about 20 s; Rust figure is an estimate, to be replaced at implementation

primary.name: distinct multisets per cell
primary.definition: number of distinct sorted degree-multisets over the k of a cell

primary.name: orbit period mismatches
primary.definition: curves whose measured x-orbit period differs from least m with lambda^m = +-1 mod l

secondary.name: positive-control partition purity
secondary.definition: fraction of positive cells whose multisets split exactly by class of kP mod d^n E(F_p) up to sign

secondary.name: negative-control false positive rate
secondary.definition: share of permuted-label datasets where the separation test rejects at alpha/4

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: every cell, every k, then stop; no interim look
a row whose polynomial degree differs from d^(2n) or whose factor degrees do not sum to it is recorded as invalid, not retried

invalidation_rules: k = 0 mod l and x(kP) at infinity are excluded by construction
a cell whose target is a critical value of phi_d^(n) (repeated root) is recorded and excluded by the pre-stated rule: discriminant nonzero over F_p

decision_rule.text: C2 supported iff n_distinct = 1 in every cell of cand-tree-k and aa-tree-k2, and the multiset equals the ref-frobenius prediction (C1). Any cell with n_distinct >= 2 falsifies the closure. C3 must hold first: the positive control must show >=2 multisets partitioned by class in every positive cell and the permutation test must reject at <= alpha/4 on the real labels and at rate <= alpha/4 on permuted labels; otherwise the verdict is invalid_measurement. C4 supported iff zero mismatches.
decision_rule.threshold: n_distinct = 1 in all cells; orbit mismatches = 0
decision_rule.statistic: max over cells of n_distinct; exact equality with the Frobenius cycle type
decision_rule.interval: none (exact); Clopper-Pearson for the control rates

graphs: S per arm per workload with the A/A interval

inadmissible: dropping or replacing a k, a curve or a cell after seeing a multiset
choosing curves where the multiset happens to agree
pooling cells with d dividing ord(P) into the prime-order arm
reading agreement at one k-pair as k-independence
quoting any of this as a cost against rho or as an attack
reading the orbit period of a non-CM curve as the CM prediction
